newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch bond contract re-start gets mixed reviews.
newsitem.headline: Dutch bond contract re-start gets mixed reviews.

text.p: Market makers involved in a project to increase liquidity in a rarely-traded Dutch bond futures contract gave it a mixed appraisal on Wednesday.
They were divided on the results to date of the attempt to generate more interest in the 10-year FTO contract. Some said it had made a good start, but others were more sceptical.
Turnover at 1100 GMT was more than 440 contracts, the highest in the three days since the renewed effort began, from a daily average of only 20 before this project started.
But some market makers said not all of the 10 banks currently involved in the project were quoting prices.
"It's quite disappointing. We were hoping for about 1,000 contracts a day in the beginning," said one trader.
"I don't think people really want to play this contract. It's hard to get in and out of, but we will put in all our efforts to make it a success."
Another trader said he detected scepticism among the market makers. But he added "I think it will work but it has to be given a long time before Dutch investors are used to it."
One market maker said turnover to date was "not bad" but the number of banks quoting prices was disappointing.
He said turnover was only among Dutch professional players with no institutions or foreign banks involved at this stage.
Another said a clear picture would not emerge for one or two months, adding he believed the project would be a success if turnover reached 2,000 contracts per day within six months.
Most investors in Dutch government bonds use the more liquid German bund futures contract to hedge their positions.
The FTO market makers are ABN AMRO, MeesPierson, Rabobank, ING, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Van Lanschot, Labouchere, AOT, NIBStrating and Bond Options.
